subject: Optimize Kit: packaging and quant/cache tradeoffs for edge inference
messages:
From: Sabrina Mendez <sabrina@edgewave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quant/cache advice for upcoming edge pilot

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for taking the meeting last week. We scoped a 6-week pilot to validate low-latency summarization on our on-prem inference cluster (NVIDIA H100 equivalent). Two asks from my side as we prepare the pilot contract:

1) High-level packaging: what Optimize Kit components do we need for an on-prem pilot vs. Hosted? We care about per-token pricing but also predictable throughput.
2) Quantization and latency: your engineering team recommended int8 + 4-bit mixed-paths during the demo — can you summarize expected latency uplift vs. fp16 and any model-quality caveats?
3) Discounts/credits: procurement is asking for a simple price concession if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool after pilot.

I attached our internal Prod QA checklist (EdgeWave_Prod_QA.pdf). Can you send a recommended commercial shape and technical notes we can attach to the SOW?

Best,
Sabrina
Director, Platform
EdgeWave

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sabrina Mendez <sabrina@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quant/cache advice for upcoming edge pilot

Hi Sabrina — thanks for the clear asks. High level below; attaching a concise tech note (OptimizeKit_TechnicalNote_v1.2.pdf) with ops-ready knobs. TL;DR: we can run the pilot with the Optimize Kit Starter + Private deployment adapter for on-prem. Suggested commercial: pilot credits + conditional commit discount.

Packaging recommendation
- Pilot: Optimize Kit Starter (includes runtime + basic monitoring), 4 pilot seats of Dedicated inference connectors, and a 3-month support window. This is the minimum to validate throughput/latency.
- Post-pilot: Reserved pool (12-month) with two commit bands: 250k tokens/month and 1M tokens/month — higher commit receives stepped discount and faster remediation SLA.

Quant & latency guidance
- fp16 baseline: best quality, modest memory footprint, higher token cost. Typical avg. p50 latency for your model shape (median seq 256) on H100-ish is ~70ms/token with our kernels.
- int8 mixed: ~1.4x token throughput vs. fp16, expected p50 ~50ms/token; small, model-dependent drop in rare-token generation quality (recommend A/B on your eval set).
- 4-bit + kernel optimizations: ~1.8–2.0x throughput; p50 ~35–40ms/token, higher variance on corner cases. Works best with models we’ve vetted for 4-bit stability in the tech note.

Batching & KV cache guidance (ops knobs)
- Continuous micro-batching (target batch 8–16 for your traffic shape) gives best latency/efficiency tradeoff. We’ll provide batching config templates matching your qps profile.
- Prefix/KV cache: large win for summarization when there are repeated system prompts or shared context; caches reduce token compute by ~20–40% depending on reuse. Cache sizing example attached.

Commercial proposal (pilot -> commit)
- Pilot: $12,000 in usage credits + 2-week free trials of Optimize Kit Starter connectors.
- Post-pilot commit options (12 months):
  * Band A: 250k tokens/mo — baseline rate (no additional discount).
  * Band B: 1M tokens/mo — 12% discount and 30% of unused pilot credits returned as additional month credit.
  * Band C: 2.5M tokens/mo — 20% discount + dedicated engineering onboarding + 3-month extended support SLA.

We can relax the commit thresholds by ~20% if you sign the SOW by 2026-12-15.

Next steps
- Karthik to add a short technical appendix clarifying throughput assumptions and fallback policy (int8->fp16).
- If commercial looks ok, we’ll draft SOW and a simple PO path for procurement.

Thanks — attaching tech note and a short cache sizing CSV.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sabrina Mendez <sabrina@edgewave.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quant/cache advice for upcoming edge pilot

Adding some technical detail so procurement and your infra folks have clarity.

Throughput/latency caveats
- Measured numbers assume steady-state KV cache hits >= 15%. If your summarization workloads have low reuse, the int8/4-bit advantages shrink.
- Int8 inference path requires per-model calibration for some decoder heads. This is low-effort for Llama-style models but can be medium-effort for highly customized finetunes. We can run a calibration pass during the pilot (2–3 hours for a typical 1B–7B tuning dataset).
- 4-bit fast path is supported on our runtime for the models listed in section 2 of the attached tech note — if your model is not on that list we will run the 4-bit stability eval during the pilot and hold a go/no-go decision.

Operational fallbacks
- Fallback policy: requests that fail 4-bit path will automatically fail over to int8 then fp16; failures are logged and surfaced in the Console. Fallbacks incur latency penalty but preserve availability.
- Autoscaling guidance: keep headroom for occasional 5–10x bursts — our autoscaler will divert traffic to Hosted fallback (if enabled) when on-prem capacity is exhausted. This is a chargeable option we can include in the SOW.

I’ll be available for a 30-min infra workshop during week 1 of the pilot to run calibration and sizing.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sabrina Mendez <sabrina@edgewave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos P. <carlos.procure@edgewave.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quant/cache advice for upcoming edge pilot

Jordan / Karthik,

Appreciate the detail — the technical appendix looks good. A few procurement questions before we proceed:

- Band B (1M tokens) is attractive but procurement is pushing for a 18% discount given their expected scale and enterprise terms (we’d also like a 99.9% latency availability SLA for the reserved pool).
- Can you confirm the exact steps and estimated hours for the calibration pass? Our infra team needs an outage-free plan.
- Legal flagged a fallback to Hosted as a data residency concern. We cannot send PII to Hosted. Is an on-prem only fallback (e.g., spare on-prem capacity or fail-queue) possible? What would that cost?

Carlos — I’ve included you to confirm what procurement needs in the SOW.

Thanks,
Sabrina

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sabrina Mendez <sabrina@edgewave.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quant/cache advice for upcoming edge pilot

Hi Sabrina — looping in commercial follow-up. We can accommodate most of EdgeWave’s asks with a single concession: an on-prem-only fallback add-on and an accelerated calibration schedule. Details below.

Commercial counteroffer
- Band B (1M tokens/mo): 15% discount (instead of 12%) if EdgeWave signs SOW by 2026-12-15. We cannot reach 18% without moving to a larger committed band.
- SLA: 99.9% service availability for the reserved on-prem pool (measured at route level) with remediation targets aligned to Band B. SLA requires a minimal dedicated on-call engineers add-on (one engineer shared across customers) — we will include this in the SOW.
- On-prem-only fallback: available as an add-on priced at a flat $6,000/month. This reserves a small cross-customer spare capacity in your region and implements a local fail-queue (no Hosted data egress).

Technical ops & calibration
- Calibration: 4 hours of calibration work (two engineers, remote) during pilot week 1; no customer-visible outage — we run calibration on a shadow set and promote once validated. We’ll provide a step-by-step ops checklist.
- Workshop: we’ll run a 90-min infra workshop (Karthik + your infra lead) to walk through batching config, KV cache sizing, and fallback tests.

Next steps
1) If this is acceptable, Jordan will circulate a revised SOW and PO template.
2) Procurement (Carlos) can review commercial terms and the DocuSign link we’ll send.
3) Schedule workshop for pilot week 0.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
